profile_text.body:
Credo AI describes itself as an AI governance platform, founded in 2020, that lets enterprises discover AI systems, enforce policies, prove compliance, and manage risk across models, agents, applications, and vendors. The company says it created the AI governance category and now focuses on what it calls Agent Governance, including a registry for agents and agentic risk controls. Its platform is built around a Knowledge Graph that combines regulatory intelligence with a customer's business context, and it offers pre-built policy packs for frameworks including the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and ISO 42001. It also offers GAIA (Govern AI Assistant), which it says is generally available in the platform.

The site says the platform covers model-level, application-level, and agent-level governance, with agents treated as governed entities that are registered, risk-assessed, sanctioned, and governed. Credo AI states that its policy packs were written by a team involved in AI governance standards work at ISO, NIST, the EU Parliament, NATO, and OECD, and that the platform draws on more than 300 integrations. The site includes customer statements attributed to Mastercard and IBM, among others, describing uses such as managing AI risk, implementing generative AI, and preparing for EU AI Act compliance.

The site's own framing is promotional, calling Credo AI the trusted leader in AI governance and saying it built its platform from scratch rather than adding AI features to a GRC tool. Beyond the company name, founding year, and website, no litigation, regulatory filings, or other third-party records are noted.
